runtimeRules.R-FEED-ORDER: Feed section order is frozen: Flash deals, then Priority placements, then Deals Near Me. Never reorderable. The three are distinct product concepts: Flash and Priority placements are promotional surfaces; Deals Near Me is proximity-led local discovery carrying nearby STANDARD, non-boosted deals only (a Standard merchant's one standard deal plus an Elite merchant's non-boosted standard deals). Merchant tier is not a filter. Proximity is node-scoped and ordered by each shop's distance from the node centre, not device geolocation.
runtimeRules.R-GRACE: A claimed code is valid until the deal expires, plus a 15-minute grace period. Never a fixed countdown from claim.
runtimeRules.R-FEE-ON-VERIFIED: The KES 30 success fee is debited only on a verified redemption, and is disclosed before it is taken.
runtimeRules.R-RESOLVE-THEN-CHARGE: Resolve the code first, then charge. Never charge before the outcome is known.
runtimeRules.R-ARREARS: Redemptions continue while a merchant owes. Arrears settle automatically from the next top-up.
runtimeRules.R-VERIFY-ANYWAY: A location mismatch still redeems. The merchant is shown the mismatch and the distance before confirming, confirms only with the customer at the counter, and the reason is recorded on the redemption; the dispute then routes to admin/Guardian review. The KES 30 fee applies because the redemption is verified — a reversal is a later, note-required admin action. Never a hard rejection.
runtimeRules.R-PHONE-BEFORE-CLAIM: An email-only account is blocked at claim until a phone number is verified.
runtimeRules.R-APPROVAL-GATE: A shop stays hidden from shoppers until an admin approves it.
runtimeRules.R-REVERSAL-NOTE: A success-fee reversal is blocked without a note. Every reversal is audit-trailed.
runtimeRules.R-LEAD-LOCK: A lead is locked to one agent for a fixed attribution window.
runtimeRules.R-AGENT-NO-SUBMIT: The agent sends an onboarding link. The merchant authenticates and submits onboarding themselves.
runtimeRules.R-VERIFY-PERMISSION: Staff need verify permission to enter codes; the owner grants it in Staff.
runtimeRules.R-STRIPE-PHASE-1: Top-up rail order is CAPABILITY-DRIVEN, not a preference: M-Pesa STK leads wherever IntaSend credentials exist, and card (Stripe Checkout) leads wherever they do not — which is every environment today, so card is the Phase 1 rail. An unprovisioned rail is never rendered as an option. And pending never means credited: a Stripe return means the checkout completed, not that the wallet moved, so the screen confirms against the real balance before it claims a credit. A card payment that has not credited yet is 'unsettled', never 'failed' — the money left the merchant's account.
runtimeRules.R-LIVE-NODES-ONLY: Only nodes flagged live are counted in founder metrics.
runtimeRules.R-VERIFIED-REDEMPTIONS: The merchant trust and ranking signal is verified redemptions. Never stars or ratings.
runtimeRules.R-ONE-PRICE: One summed YOU PAY number, identical on tile, detail and claimed code. Extra charges are declared up front and cannot be added at the counter.
runtimeRules.R-PLAN-NAMES: Plans are Standard and Elite, never Free. Success fee KES 30, Elite KES 3,500/month, boost KES 500/24h.
runtimeRules.R-TAGLINE: Tagline is exact: Discover, Claim and Redeem.

frames.name: Verify-phone gate
frames.job: Bind a verified phone to an email-only account before the shopper can claim anything.

frames.name: Deal feed
frames.job: Find a live deal worth walking to. Flash deals and Priority placements lead; Deals Near Me carries nearby standard deals so the default discovery rail is proximity-led.
frames.captureReadinessReason: Marketplace density is seeded during Node 0 rehearsal.
frames.notes: Section order is R-FEED-ORDER and is read from FEED_SECTIONS in src/lib/feed-sections.ts, so the labels live in one place. Deals Near Me is ordered by orderNearMeDeals (located shops nearest-first, then unlocated newest-first) and its subtitle drops the proximity claim when the node has no coordinates.

frames.primaryAction: Open a deal from the map
frames.captureReadinessReason: Map pins depend on seeded geo data.

frames.name: Deal detail
frames.job: Decide whether the deal is worth it, seeing the full price before committing.
frames.captureReadinessReason: Deal content is seeded rehearsal data.

frames.name: Claimed code

frames.captureReadinessReason: Example-code framing must not read as a real claimable code.

frames.captureReadinessReason: Claim history is seeded rehearsal data.

frames.name: Redeem at counter

frames.name: Staff verify gate
frames.job: Tell staff without permission why they cannot verify, and who can fix it.
frames.captureReadinessReason: Shows staff permission state and owner contact details.

frames.name: Wallet — arrears
frames.job: Know exactly what is owed and what happens next.
frames.captureReadinessReason: Shows money owed by a named merchant.

frames.name: Top-up
frames.job: Add balance so success fees can be paid.
frames.notes: Rail order is capability-driven (R-STRIPE-PHASE-1), so the screen is now smoke-eligible on its heading: 'Top up' is stable whichever rail leads, and asserting it locks in no primary method. States: `amount` is the form; `card-checkout` is Stripe-hosted, so the app owns the hand-off and both returns rather than the page itself; `pending` is the `confirming` screen, which polls for BOTH rails; `credited` renders the observed balance delta. A charged card that has not credited lands on `unsettled` — 'Payment received', never the failure screen.
frames.captureReadinessReason: Live payment credentials are still pending for both rails, so amounts are sandbox.

frames.name: Alerts
frames.job: Catch wallet and deal problems before they cost a redemption.

frames.name: My deals
frames.job: See what is live and what it actually earned.

drift.what: RESOLVED 2026-07-29 — verify-anyway is correct; the frames were wrong
drift.detail: Founder ruling 2026-07-29: a location mismatch still redeems and the dispute goes to admin. The frames and prototype showed wrong-shop as a hard rejection with no fee — that branch is superseded and must not be built. The shipped code already implemented the correct behaviour: preflight returns locationMismatch + distance, the keypad discloses it as a warning and records a reason on confirm, and Guardian (13e) receives the dispute. No code change was required.

drift.detail: The mirror now lives at maanta-app/design/current-reality/ (frames.json + frames.schema.json + this README) and Layer 1 runs on every PR via npm run test:design-truth, so "the repo validates the contract" is no longer aspiration. Layer 1 caught five stale references on its first run; all are recorded under landedInRepo.corrections.

drift.what: DECIDED 2026-07-29 — the third feed section is Deals Near Me
drift.detail: Founder decision: the third section is named Deals Near Me and carries nearby standard deals only. The rationale is behavioural — shoppers engage with deals in the area they are in or travelling to, so the default standard rail is proximity-led while Flash and Priority placements stay separate promotional surfaces. The repo briefly rendered 'All active deals', which is now superseded. The bucket query already returned exactly the right class of deal (deal_type = standard AND boost_active = false); what changed is the label, an explicit proximity ordering, and an honest subtitle.

The mirror recorded frames 8af/8ag as having no matching route. Both see-all links resolve: the feed links /search?type=flash and /search?type=boosted, and the search page queries both (deal_type = flash; boost_active = true). The filter sheet gained a Boosted option so the arriving state is representable. No dedicated see-all ROUTE was built and none is needed — /search with a type parameter is the shipped destination.

The mirror recorded the archive frame with repost as not found in the codebase. /merchant/deals/archived lists the last five expired deals and renders Repost / Delete via archived-actions.tsx; both writes are real and permission-gated with requireMerchant("can_deals"). The buttons render only for users holding can_deals.

drift.what: CLOSED 2026-07-29 — the Elite 2-deal limit is enforced
drift.detail: The mirror recorded the limit as stated across frames with enforcement not confirmed in the repo. It is enforced in Postgres by the enforce_deal_limit trigger: standard -> deal_limit 1, elite -> 2, counted over deals WHERE is_active = TRUE, raising when active_count >= deal_limit; flash on Standard raises separately. src/lib/deal-limits.ts mirrors the same rule in the UI so the merchant is blocked before filling in the wizard rather than at publish.

The mirror recorded the frames modelling four permissions against a coarser repo gate. merchant_staff carries all four booleans (can_verify default TRUE, can_deals/can_topup/can_purchase default FALSE), requireMerchant("can_*") enforces each on the server, and src/lib/merchant-nav.ts maps each one to the entry points it gates so nav and guards cannot disagree.

drift.what: CLOSED 2026-07-29 — rail order is capability-driven, and pending no longer reads as credited
drift.detail: The mirror recorded a mismatch between the design system (M-Pesa always primary) and shipped code (Stripe Phase 1). There is no longer a code question: isMpesaTopupConfigured() reads the real INTASEND_API_KEY / INTASEND_SECRET, so M-Pesa leads the moment credentials exist and card leads until then, and an unprovisioned rail is not rendered at all. Closing the row surfaced the real defect behind it: the card rail rendered the green success takeover on Stripe's redirect with added: 0 and the pre-payment balance, claiming a credit the webhook had not made, and it never polled — so its 'credited' state could not render. Both are fixed. What remains is live payment credentials, which is an ops task needing no code.

drift.what: CLOSED 2026-07-29 — pricing copy is governed; the launch offer is withdrawn
drift.detail: Founder decision: treat 'Launch offer: first month of Elite free' as WITHDRAWN until a governed launch offer exists. The line is removed from /pricing and no duplicate surface carries it. The four closing conditions all hold: R-PLAN-NAMES is satisfied, the Standard plan is never labelled 'Free' (it reads 'No monthly fee'), the KES 30 success fee is visible beside the Standard card, and no ungoverned launch-offer promise remains — asserted by src/__tests__/cash-only-and-copy.test.ts. The 11e half of this row was never drift: admin support is a desktop ops surface deliberately outside the phone prototype, and both its states ship. A future Elite launch offer must be backed by config/policy before it is re-advertised.
